A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GCA/DRT research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: Tables 1-3 report original language-modeling, summarization, retrieval, and inference-efficiency results, supplemented by ablations and retrieval case studies.

after.justification: The original empirical results are retained, and Table 4 adds training-throughput and memory measurements across model sizes.

M1.justification: Equation 1 changes the stated retrieval-scoring procedure from a direct landmark dot product to one incorporating W_h^g and W_l linear projections. GCA fusion, Gumbel sampling, and inference offloading remain unchanged.

E1.justification: PG19, arXiv-math, XSum, CNN/DailyMail, single-passkey retrieval, and two-hop retrieval are retained. The renamed two-hop test matches the earlier results and discussion; the new model-size efficiency measurements do not establish additional dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: New Table 4 evaluates a full-attention Transformer comparator alongside sliding-window Transformers, BRT, and the authors' RPT implementation. Comparator membership in the retained Tables 1-3 is unchanged.

E3.justification: Table 4 adds throughput and memory evaluation at 350M/32K, 760M/16K, 1.5B/8K, and 3B/4K parameter/context configurations. Appendix D newly documents existing NIAH settings without establishing that those experiments changed or were rerun.

E4.justification: Table 4 extends the efficiency analysis to how training throughput and memory requirements vary across model scales. The existing component ablations, length-extrapolation plots, and main-text and appendix retrieval case studies remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. The added efficiency results retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: All numerical results in Tables 1-3 and the Figure 3 plots are retained. New Table 4 reports additional efficiency results: at 350M/32K, DRT retrieval×1 has throughput 2.32×10^5 and memory 56G, versus 4.44×10^4 and 50G for the full-attention Transformer.

T1.justification: Equation 1 substantively revises the mathematical relevance-score definition by introducing linear mappings. Equation 2's index rearrangement is not substantive; the remaining attention mathematics, complexity analysis, and appendix algorithms are unchanged.

C1.justification: The principal claims about end-to-end causal retrieval, efficient GCA/DRT modeling, and perfect passkey retrieval at 16M tokens with 1000-fold length generalization are retained. The added future-work proposals are not presented as achieved contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 and Table 2 qualify the evaluations as tasks 'akin to RULER,' replacing direct RULER attribution and narrowing what the scores represent. Section 5 adds prospective external-context and structured retrieval directions; existing mechanism explanations and RPT-baseline qualifications remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-release pointer and Appendix D's NIAH checkpoint source, synthetic examples, fine-tuning duration, and landmark-aligned input padding. Conversely, Appendix A removes the specific 350M architecture details previously supplied; this does not establish an architecture change.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to Infini-attention, Expansion Span, and two Hu et al. 2024 structured-representation papers. It also explicitly contrasts GCA's joint training without external models against RPT, while retaining the main research positioning.

P1.justification: The revision makes limited copyedits, changes 'long-context' terminology to 'long-range,' and updates correspondence and publication text. It adds future-work and impact paragraphs, removes the empty 'Results for larger models' appendix heading, and renumbers retained appendices.

P2.justification: v3 redraws Figure 2, adds Tables 4 and 5, updates Table 2's task and model-size labels, and relocates existing displays. Table 1 loses its 32K evaluation-block heading despite retaining that block's results; the other figures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Appendix D makes the headline NIAH results easier to assess by documenting synthetic examples, fine-tuning, and landmark-aligned padding. The code pointer and Table 4 add useful reproducibility information and efficiency evidence. These limited gains outweigh the omitted 350M architecture details and missing 32K table heading; the principal accuracy evidence remains unchanged.
